title: KaMPIng: Flexible and (Near) Zero-Overhead C++ Bindings for MPI
problem: MPI only provides C and Fortran bindings, not native C++ support, preventing developers from leveraging modern C++ features for safe and rapid development in high-performance computing applications.
motivation: C++ and MPI are foundational to HPC, but the lack of native C++ bindings forces developers to use unsafe low-level C interfaces or unreliable third-party wrappers, missing opportunities for faster and less error-prone development.
method: The library provides C++ bindings at multiple abstraction levels from low-level MPI calls to STL-style interfaces using named parameters. Template metaprogramming is exploited to generate only required code paths at compile time, achieving near-zero overhead. A flexible type system and additional safety guarantees prevent programming errors.
key_novelty: Using C++ named parameters and template metaprogramming to create zero-overhead, high-level STL-style MPI bindings where most parameters are automatically inferred.
contributions: C++ language bindings covering multiple abstraction levels from low-level to STL-style convenient APIs
Named parameter design enabling intuitive MPI interfaces with parameter inference
Near-zero overhead through compile-time template metaprogramming and selective code generation
Type system with safety guarantees to prevent distributed computing programming errors

metrics.other: Application benchmarks on sorting algorithms and phylogenetic inference
